entries.title: YouTube might offer Audiobooks in 2027
entries.summary: According to a report by The Wall Street Journal, YouTube is “looking” into audiobooks for a future addition to the app. The post YouTube might offer Audiobooks in 2027 first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
YouTube is reportedly in talks with major book publishers to launch an official audiobook feature that could debut as early as 2027. According to a report by The Wall Street Journal, Google is exploring ways to expand its ecosystem and is considering bundling the new feature into its existing YouTube Premium subscription, which currently costs $15.99 per month in the U.S.

There is a serious piracy problem on YouTube right now. There are a copious number of channels with audiobook videos on the platform if you look. Some feature public-domain titles, but others offer books that aren’t legally allowed on YouTube. The existing system to ensure a piece of work belongs to the uploader doesn’t really apply to audiobooks, so it’s the virtual Wild West.

Edison data shows that 45% of listeners have consumed an audiobook on YouTube (up from 35% previously), making it a major distribution channel—often filled with low-quality robotic voices. Similar pirated AI audiobooks also bleed into platforms like Spotify, disguised as podcasts.

YouTube will have its work cut out for it, since competition is already firmly entrenched. Spotify offers a variety of plans. Premium subscriptions include 15 hours of audiobook listening per month; for an additional $12 per month, you can add another 15 hours with the Audiobooks+ add-on. A standalone Audio Access plan is also available for $10 a month, which provides 15 hours each month. Additionally, individual audiobooks can be purchased through the Spotify Web Player.

On the other hand, Audible’s Standard membership costs $9 per month, granting you access to one audiobook each month from its collection as long as you maintain your subscription. For $15 a month, the Premium membership gives you one monthly credit for a title you can keep indefinitely, plus access to a vast catalog for unlimited listening.

Everand (formerly Scribd) offers a flat-fee monthly subscription, around $11.99 per month, providing unlimited-style access to audiobooks, eBooks, and magazines, though heavy use of trending titles can face throttling. Amazon Kindle Unlimited, Kobo Plus, and even the public library all offer audiobooks.

entries.title: US E-book revenue was down 5.7% in August 2026
entries.summary: E-book revenues were down 5.7% to $83.9 million for the month, and revenues from Digital Audiobooks were up 12.6% in August, coming in at $105.4 million. The post US E-book revenue was down 5.7% in August 2026 first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
E-book revenues were down 5.7% to $83.9 million for the month, and revenues from Digital Audiobooks were up 12.6% in August, coming in at $105.4 million. Physical Audio revenues were down 35.2%, coming in at $400 thousand. Year-to-date E-Book revenues were down 3.4% compared to 2025, generating $685.1 million. Digital Audiobook revenue was up 12.6% to $806.3 million, while Physical Audio revenue was down 11.9% to $3.5 million.

In terms of physical formats during the month of August, Hardback revenues were up 13.8%, coming in at $320.2 million; Paperbacks were up 17.6%, with $333.3 million in revenue; Mass Market was down 14.6% to $6.2 million; and Special Bindings were up 3.7%, with $20.4 million in revenue.

Hardback revenues were up 3.1% year-to-date to $2.1 billion; Paperbacks were up 11.8% to $2.3 billion; Mass Market was down 57.2% to $26.9 million; and Special Bindings were up 14.5% to $152.6 million.

entries.title: Libro.fm e-books are pushed back until 2027
entries.summary: Libro.fm has admitted that their new e-book platform will not go live until 2027, but further details will be announced by the end of 2026. The post Libro.fm e-books are pushed back until 2027 first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Libro.fm is an audiobook subscription platform that allows users to purchase audiobooks while financially supporting a designated local independent bookstore. The company has confirmed in a new FAQ that its new e-book platform will launch sometime in 2027, after initially saying it would be available in 2026.

They stated that “Our bookselling partners will gain access to ebooks this fall, and we’ll share updates on wider availability as we approach 2027. All of our audiobooks will remain DRM-free, and we are working to bring on as many DRM-free ebooks as possible. Unfortunately, publisher terms won’t always allow that. Access to DRM-free ebooks matters, and we promise not only to keep encouraging our publishing partners to offer DRM-free reads, but also to do what we can to make these books as accessible as possible in the meantime. Credits can be used to purchase audiobooks or ebooks. However, Ebooks can also be purchased à la carte.”

The company will also support a number of e-book readers. “We are working to make our ebooks as accessible as possible, which includes the ability to read them on different e-readers and apps. While we can’t confirm the extent of e-reader compatibility yet, we’ll share clear information as we near launch. The best reading experience, including features like LibroSync, will be available in the Libro apps.”

It would be nice if they added Kobo to the list, since many other companies are starting to work with them, such as the Cloud Library.

entries.title: Crunchyroll Manga launches in Australia and New Zealand
entries.summary: The manga service has also just launched in the United Kingdom, Ireland, Australia, New Zealand, India, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka. The post Crunchyroll Manga launches in Australia and New Zealand first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Crunchyroll Manga has launched in Australia and New Zealand with more than 250 English-language titles from publishers including J-Novel Club, Square Enix, and Yen Press. The library includes The Apothecary Diaries, My Dress-Up Darling, Bocchi the Rock!, Bungo Stray Dogs, Delicious in Dungeon, Lycoris Recoil, and Sasaki and Miyano, among plenty of others.

The manga service has also just launched in the United Kingdom, Ireland, Australia, New Zealand, India, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan and Sri Lanka.

The revised Crunchyroll Manga launched in the US and Canada in October 2025 and has since grown to more than 450 titles, with books from publishers including Kodansha, Shueisha, VIZ Media, Square Enix, and Yen Press. To read the manga, you must subscribe to Crunchyroll. You can read the content on iOS, Android, and the web.

entries.title: Audible Will Launch New Features to Bring Listeners Into the Story
entries.summary: Audible is taking a leap into immersive experiences, allowing listeners to dive deeper into character journeys, gain unique insights into stories, and even step into the narrative themselves. The post Audible Will Launch New Features to Bring Listeners Into the Story first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Last week, Audible introduced an exciting range of immersive features aimed at enhancing the way listeners engage with audiobooks. Over the coming months, the audiobook giant will be rolling out three innovative features: the Character Guide, Interactive Stories, and Visual Explorer. These enhancements will be linked to some of our upcoming multi-cast productions and Audible Originals, including classics like Dracula and George Orwell’s 1984, as well as the original Exoplanet, produced by Andy Weir and written by Benjamin Percy.

“AI is allowing us to create new interactive experiences that today’s listeners, especially younger audiences, are craving. We are opening up entry points into stories that are still part of the authors’ vision, but that make our customers’ experiences more personal and unique,” Andy Tsao, Chief Product and Analytics Officer at Audible.

Character Guide: is now available and featured on Audible Originals! This innovative tool addresses a familiar challenge for audiobook listeners – keeping track of a large cast of characters. As you enjoy your story, Character Guide highlights which character is currently speaking, making it easier to follow along. Plus, for those curious about the talented actors behind the voices, the player page includes narrator headshots and bios, enriching your listening experience!

Interactive Stories: Dive into a new dimension of storytelling with the recently launched Dracula (see above). This exciting feature enables listeners to engage in real-time dialogues with characters from the narrative. By merging generative AI, conversational design, and immersive sound production, listeners are assigned a role and a mission, and the stakes rise as the character initiates the conversation. You respond in your own words, and the character reacts on the spot. Mark your calendar for November 5, when the next Interactive Story will transport you to the universe of the Audible Original Exoplanet, crafted in collaboration with author Benjamin Percy.

Visual Explorer: The latest addition is the Visual Explorer feature, which enhances the listening experience by providing relevant images and visual context. This could include a map highlighting the story’s location, artwork connected to the narrative, and more. By integrating visuals with audio, it caters to the growing trend among today’s listeners who crave a more immersive experience. Featured in Audible’s The Cultural Tutor’s Grand Tour: The Story of Europe in Six Cities, this feature allows listeners to delve into extra imagery and informative content about significant landmarks, figures, and places across six European cities.

At the moment, these features are being introduced in a limited beta version for Audible users in the U.S. and U.K. The company plans to gather customer feedback to refine and improve these features as they expand to additional markets.

entries.title: Would you buy Amazon Kids e-readers in 2026?
entries.summary: Have you purchased an Amazon Kids e-reader before, or do you plan to pick up the latest 13th-generation device? The post Would you buy Amazon Kids e-readers in 2026? first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Amazon Kindle Kids is a line of e-readers built specifically for children to encourage reading without digital distractions. While the device itself uses the exact same premium, eye-strain-free e-ink hardware as standard adult Kindles, it is packaged as a kid-friendly bundle with dedicated parental software.

Every device includes a durable, artist-designed protective cover and a 1-year subscription to Amazon Kids+, giving children unlimited access to thousands of age-appropriate books, series, and audiobooks. Through the Amazon Parent Dashboard mobile app, parents can monitor reading progress, set daily educational goals, establish bedtimes, and approve which books from their own library can be shared with the child. The software includes features like Word Wise (which automatically displays short, simple definitions above difficult words) and an automatic Vocabulary Builder to help kids learn as they read.

Amazon Kindle Kids in 2026

Amazon refreshed its entire e-reader lineup, introducing three brand-new Kindle Kids models. Every device in this new generation features an edge-to-edge flush display and thinner, lighter hardware. The defining benefit of the Kids line remains its bundle value: each e-reader includes an artist-designed protective case, an ad-free experience, a 2-year worry-free replacement guarantee, and 12 months of Amazon Kids+, which grants access to thousands of age-appropriate books and audiobooks.

The latest lineup of Amazon Kids Kindles offers an excellent, distraction-free reading experience that easily outclasses standard tablets for bedtime and focus. With a refreshed lineup that includes a lighter base Kindle, a waterproof 7-inch Paperwhite Kids, and a new, vibrant Colorsoft Kids, there is a perfect hardware match for every age group, from early readers to comic-loving teens. The core magic remains Amazon’s software and bundle ecosystem: the inclusion of a sturdy, kid-friendly case, a 2-year worry-free replacement guarantee, and a year of Amazon Kids+ makes the upfront cost highly economical. Parents will especially love the Parent Dashboard, which lets them set reading goals and bedtimes while completely locking out games, videos, and social media notifications.

The primary trade-off across the 2026 lineup comes down to price versus specialized features. While the base model is incredibly compact and affordable for traditional chapter books, upgrading to the Paperwhite Kids is highly recommended for younger or messier kids due to its robust IPX8 waterproofing and soothing adjustable warm light. Meanwhile, the premium Colorsoft Kids is a major win for graphic novel and comic enthusiasts, though its higher price point may be hard to justify if your child mostly reads black-and-white text. Overall, these e-readers are a stellar investment in literacy, providing a premium, eye-strain-free digital library that grows seamlessly alongside your child’s reading skills.



Wrap Up

Have you purchased a Kindle Kids in 2026 or in the past? I like that they come with a free case, and instead of the typical one-year warranty, they come with two. I know many people who bought the Kindle Kids for themselves, not for a child, because of the sheer amount of content it comes with. Or are you waiting for Black Friday to get one?

entries.title: Calibre added support for reading images in the AVIF format
entries.summary: Calibre now supports the AVIF image format, enabling Amazon to adopt it for book covers. The post Calibre added support for reading images in the AVIF format first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Calibre natively added support for reading images in the AVIF format as part of its Calibre 9.16.0 release. The e-book manager can now read, render, and process AVIF images internally. This is especially helpful as platforms like Amazon have increasingly adopted .avif for book cover delivery.

In mid-September, Amazon changed some product images across all properties from PNG or JPEG to .avif. This also affects Kindle Book cover art and Kindle e-reader images. AVIF is a modern, open-source, and royalty-free image file format used to store still and animated images with much smaller file sizes than traditional formats like JPEG or PNG. The Alliance for Open Media (a group including tech giants like Google, Netflix, Amazon, and Microsoft) developed it and first released it in 2019. The format improves site loading speeds, which is why Amazon is slowly adopting it.

entries.title: Why did Amazon ditch the Fire name for their tablets?
entries.summary: Amazon has retired the Kindle Fire and Fire Tablets. using Alexa Tablets. What are the main differences between Fire Tablets and Alexa Tablets? The post Why did Amazon ditch the Fire name for their tablets? first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Amazon first released its tablets under the Kindle Fire name in November 2011. Amazon dropped the “Kindle” part of the name in September 2014 with the release of its fourth-generation tablets, renaming them simply as Fire tablets, such as the Fire HD and Fire HDX. Amazon dropped the Fire tablet branding in October 2026 to replace its budget-focused line with new, higher-priced Alexa Tablets that run full Android with Google Play access.

Amazon introduced the new Alexa Tablet 8, Alexa Tablet 11, and Alexa Tablet 12 Pro, which are priced higher, ranging from $229.99 to $549.99. Unlike old Fire tablets that used custom Fire OS and the limited Amazon Appstore, the new Alexa Tablets

run standard Android and feature full access to the Google Play Store. If you currently own a Fire tablet, Amazon will continue providing security and operating system updates for at least four years after the final shipment date.

Amazon Alexa Tablet 12 Pro

Amazon Alexa Tablet 12 Pro is the most advanced tablet we’ve ever built. Stamped from a single piece of aluminum, it measures just 6.5 mm thick, is super lightweight, and is engineered for perfect balance. It houses a 12-inch, 280 PPI display, a 120Hz refresh rate, and a 3:2 aspect ratio for more usable screen space—perfect for reading, watching, or working. The Amazon Alexa Tablet 12 Pro comes in two display options: a vibrant standard display and a cutting-edge Nanomatte display with anti-glare.

Powered by a 4nm 8-core chip with up to 16GB of RAM, the Amazon Alexa Tablet 12 Pro delivers nearly three times faster processing and nine times faster graphics than any tablet we’ve ever shipped—handling everything from multi-window multitasking to graphic-intensive gaming and 4K streaming. With quad Dolby Atmos speakers, Wi-Fi 6E, and 16 hours of video playback—the longest we’ve ever put on a tablet—it provides all-day power. The Nanomatte model goes further, with even more processing power and up to 16GB of RAM.

Amazon Alexa Tablet 11

The new Amazon Alexa Tablet 11—an 11-inch device with a 2.5K display at 276 pixels per inch, 90Hz smooth scrolling, and a 16:10 cinematic aspect ratio—is designed for streaming, gaming, reading, and browsing. A thin aluminum unibody houses an 8-core processor with 8GB of RAM, dual Dolby Atmos speakers, and up to 15 hours of video playback. Alexa+ is built in with the same Dynamic Tab, voice and touch access, and personalized intelligence. Available in Graphite, Amethyst, and Matcha.

Amazon Alexa Tablet 8

The new Amazon Alexa Tablet 8 is the most portable tablet in the lineup, with an 8.7-inch display in an all-aluminum design that weighs just 329g. At 7.95mm thick, it’s designed to fit in one hand and carry anywhere, making it ideal for reading, browsing, and streaming on the go. It’s powered by an 8-core processor with Wi-Fi 6, up to 14 hours of video playback, and built-in Alexa+ intelligence. Available in Graphite, Rosette, and Teal.

entries.title: Goodreads finally supports half-star ratings
entries.summary: You can now rate books on Goodreads from 0.25 to 5.0 stars (including popular intermediate values like 3.5, 4.5, 3.75, and 4.25). The post Goodreads finally supports half-star ratings first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Goodreads officially supports both half-star (0.5) and quarter-star (0.25) ratings. The feature launched in early October 2026 after more than a decade of user requests. In less than two days after the launch of half and quarter stars, the Goodreads community added 3.5 million book ratings across the site. The four most-used new star ratings so far are, in order: 3.5, 4.5, 3.75, and 4.25.

However, all of your historic whole-star ratings remain exactly as they were. They will remain unchanged unless you want to go back and re-rate dozens to hundreds of books. Kindle integration allows users to sync or refine their ratings on the Goodreads platform after reading.

The new rating system might be too late for Goodreads. Many people on social media have voiced concerns: “I think ‘why now’ is because enough people have left Goodreads and moved to other reading trackers that it’s finally hurting them, so they’re scrambling to finally implement these features and get people back.”

“I’ve never understood why people were so feral about wanting half-stars. And quarter stars?? That’s just too many. The 5-star system works fine.”

This new system has been a bit buggy from the start. The Goodreads desktop app doesn’t support the new stars yet, but Goodreads hasn’t prioritized it in a long time.

entries.title: Google launched Expert Intelligence on Google Play Books
entries.summary: The platform launched with over 100,000 titles; the integration lets users generate quizzes, infographics, and Audio Overviews while combining published books with personal notes. The post Google launched Expert Intelligence on Google Play Books first appeared on Good e-Reader.
entries.content:
Google launched Expert Intelligence, a cross-product AI initiative that lets you add eligible e-books purchased from Google Play Books directly into Gemini Notebook as grounded sources. The platform launched with over 100,000 titles; the integration lets users generate quizzes, infographics, and Audio Overviews while combining published books with personal notes.

Expert Intelligence launched a month ago with more than 100,000 books from major publishers, including Bloomsbury, De Gruyter Brill, Johns Hopkins University Press, Macmillan Publishers, O’Reilly Media, and Penguin Random House. Google also collaborated closely with more than 15 bestselling authors — including Steven Pinker, Michael Pollan, and Jennifer Wallace — to curate special Featured Notebooks that supplement their books with additional sources and engaging artifacts that let readers dive deeper into the author’s work.

You can see if a book is eligible for Expert Intelligence by visiting Google Play Books. If eligible, you’ll see Gemini Notebook listed when you click the “Tools” badge on a book’s detail page. To get you started, they’re also providing a book for people in the U.S. while supplies last. In the future, people will also be able to add more sources, such as third-party subscriptions, business research reports, and textbooks.
